slides.heading: HIGH ANGLE VS LOW ANGLE
slides.subheading: Choose angle based on the character's emotional state.

slides.heading: WHY IT MATTERS
bullets: High angles diminish subjects; low angles empower them—angle changes meaning.
A high angle makes a subject look small, vulnerable, or overwhelmed.
A low angle makes them look strong, dominant, or heroic.

slides.heading: ANGLE MEANING
slides.caption: Raise or lower the camera to reinforce power, vulnerability, or neutrality.

slides.heading: HOW TO CHOOSE ANGLE
steps: Decide what the scene says about the subject.
Raise or lower the camera accordingly.

slides.heading: PRO TIP
slides.text: Low angles with wide lenses exaggerate power.

slides.heading: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.text: Using eye level for every shot.
